propagation.finding: The first delivery audit (Round 1) had 1/9 correct claims. This audit (Round 2) has 2/6 correct + 2 new failure modes (FABRICATED, HALF-TRUTH). The vinculum deletion test is working — each round exposes more overstatement. But the failure MODES are evolving, not resolving.

Same pattern as the sieve: the parametric identity (keyword matching) solves 100% of the trivial corridor (finding 'any weapons'), but the hard corridor (plan-specific requirements) remains unsolved. The real problem is never the easy search — it's the constraint matching.

CP6 (real PBR) is mod9=4 GREEN — the only genuinely correct delivery. CP4 (wrong genre) is mod9=0 INFRA — self-destructive, actively harmful (wrong assets committed). CP5 (partial match) is mod9=3 YELLOW — caution, works partially but overclaimed.

The dependency chain CP6→CP7→CP1-5 means the ONE correct delivery (CP6 materials) is the root hypha. Fix CP6 properly and CP7 (crafting) becomes viable. The other CPs are leaf nodes that can be regenerated.

EXTRUDE (x2): Double down on CP6 wiring — it's the only verified win. BEVEL (x3): NEVER download before verifying plan match. PAINT (x7): The 5 lessons learned above should become a reusable pre-download checklist.
730 files → ~100 plan-usable = 7.3x noise. The first-pass download strategy generated 86% waste. A pre-filter step would reduce this to near-zero waste.
